title: Metaform Graph Model
description: The JSON object is the functional namespace. Elements occupy nested paths. Each element owns its properties and native knowledge arrays. dependencies holds the dependencies of the receiving element as an array of records. Each record names its providing element in pe, a project-relative address. Each providing element also exists at its own nested path. Tool command addresses do not replace this stored tree.

NamespaceValue.title: Value at a namespace address
NamespaceValue.description: Objects extend the addressed hierarchy or hold structured data. Arrays denote composed element layers; scalars are direct values.

NamespaceNode.title: Namespace branch or receiving element
NamespaceNode.description: Namespace branch or receiving element. Its properties and layers are directly on the element. The same word can name metadata or a namespace branch according to its value and context.

anyOf.description: The name used for this functionality in project documentation or specifications, such as Metaform.

The element's role in the intake: AT (Artifact Type, the type that groups the artifacts examined), DE (Defining Element, whose loss would prevent the artifact from remaining the same type), SE (Supportive Element, whose Encounter Function helps a Defining Element serve the purpose of the CQU), NE (Notable Element, which states an essential demand or requirement), CQU (Cestui Que Use, the party outside the artifact whose purpose drives improvement of it), UD (Upstream Dependency, an element outside the artifact that an element depends on) or DD (Downstream Dependant, an element outside the artifact that depends on it and is not a person). A map may hold several Defining Elements.

Implementation state. Use un_built for intended functionality not yet built. Legacy missing/todo spellings and intake BKN/broken judgments are not accepted. Other lifecycle state names are not defined by this schema.

The well-understood practitioner short name derived from the leaf segments. Must exactly match the same number of leading words of the reversed, space-separated namespace address, and must not match `name`.
Optional project metadata; does not introduce a required wrapper.

The source links for this element: one uri for each artifact that has this address. A code project is one artifact, so it has one uri, the entry point for this functionality. When several artifacts share the address, such as photos of one type, list the uri of each. A relative file path is allowed.

providers.description: This word may name a namespace branch. The functional relationships are in dependencies, not providers.

propertyNames.description: One namespace segment, never a dotted reference or JSONPath expression.

ComposedElementLayer.title: Array-valued composed element layer
ComposedElementLayer.description: An array at an element is a knowledge layer. Its members retain their native formats and nesting. Do not reinterpret fields inside native members as functional namespace branches.

Dependencies.title: Dependencies
Dependencies.description: The dependencies this receiving element holds: a list with one record for each providing element.

DependencyRecord.title: Dependency record
DependencyRecord.description: One dependency of this receiving element: the providing element (pe), what the receiver seeks through it (op), how the provider serves that purpose (ef) and the direction of the flow (ifd). These four are one set. A providing element appears once in the list.

pe.description: The address of the Providing Element (PE): the element whose Encounter Function serves this receiving element's Operative Purpose. It refers to the actual element in the nested tree, which keeps its own fields at its own location.

op.description: What this receiver seeks to accomplish through this provider. This is its Operative Purpose (OP). Use clear, simple technical English.

ef.description: How this provider serves this receiver's goal in this encounter. This is its Encounter Function (EF). Use clear, simple technical English.

ifd.description: The Information Flow Direction (IFD): the direction of the movement of substance that satisfies the receiver's Operative Purpose, relative to the receiver and not including the request: send, receive or both.

RelationshipWord.description: This word may name a namespace branch or native layer. The fields pe, op, ef and ifd belong inside a dependency record, not on the element.

$comment: Owner-authorized terminology and tool-contract update, 2026-10-31. This schema validates one selected project namespace. A host may store it below a project key. Provider addresses resolve from that selected project, not from the host root. validate_metaform.py also checks reference resolution, duplicate relationships and name_length bounds. MCP command input has a separate schema. Validation does not prove functional reasoning. CQU and the authored concepts remain in force.
